pages.text: Today the herd would leave for a distant waterhole! Moya bounced beside the red dirt path. "Let's go!" Mom asked, "All ready?" "Yes!" Moya started to race away.
Mom gently nudged Moya's slim tummy. It only rumbled. "An empty tummy?" In their excitement, Moya had forgotten water and grass. "Can't we just go?" Moya pouted.
Mom asked, "What if you're thirsty along the way and there's no water?" Moya imagined a sun-baked field, a dry throat, and a rumbling tummy. "I wouldn't like that..."
Mom lowered her neck. "On the grassland, your tummy is your bag. Put what you need inside, one thing at a time. Shall we count?" Tumba passed, round tummy forward. "Mine's packed already!"
Mom pointed with her muzzle to the waterhole, the grass, and the place beside her. "These three will get us ready." Moya followed. "Water, grass, beside Mom!"
"Let's put them in, one at a time!" Mom whispered. Moya bent over the waterhole. First, a gulp of water.
Moya took a mouthful of grass, then stood beside Mom. Together they counted. "One, water! Two, grass! Three, beside Mom! Before a long journey!" Moya's tummy grew round.
Water sloshed in Moya's full tummy. They stretched their neck toward the far end of the path. "Nothing missing now!" Tumba grinned. "Your tummy's as round as mine!"
Now Moya knew the journey steps. "One, water! Two, grass! Three, beside Mom!" Next time, Moya bent to drink before Mom said a word. Gulp, munch, ready!
Mom rested her chin on Moya's back. "Our journey-ready champion!" Counting each thing meant nothing was forgotten. Before a long journey! Moya walked close beside Mom along the red dirt path.
